title: Coast Guard, FBI Boarded Two Texas-Bound Tankers After Cyberattacks
excerpt: The August 21 and 24 boardings followed suspected breaches of the ships' networks near the Strait of Gibraltar; officials are probing a possible Iran link but have not named a culprit.
body:
• Coast Guard and FBI cyber teams boarded two foreign-flagged tankers bound for Texas on August 21 and 24 after signs their networks had been compromised by overseas cyber actors.
  • The first vessel, the Liberian-flagged VLCC VL Prosperity, was carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude from Egypt to Galveston; the second, the Kohaku, was an LPG tanker bound for a Texas port.
  • The breaches occurred while both ships transited the Strait of Gibraltar in early August; one ship reportedly lost communications for 30 hours.
  • The U.S. is investigating a possible Iran link, though officials have not publicly attributed the attacks; crews cooperated and no operational or environmental damage was reported.

The U.S. Coast Guard and FBI quietly boarded two foreign-flagged commercial tankers bound for Texas last month after indications that their networks had been compromised by overseas cyber actors, U.S. officials confirmed this week. The boardings — on August 21 and 24 in the Gulf of Mexico — mark one of the most serious maritime cybersecurity incidents involving energy shipping off the American coast.

The first vessel boarded was the VL Prosperity, a 333-meter Liberian-flagged very large crude carrier carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude from Egypt's Sidi Kerir terminal to Galveston, Texas, the Wall Street Journal reported. The second, the Kohaku, was a liquefied petroleum gas tanker bound for another Texas port. Neither the Coast Guard nor the FBI has officially named the ships; the identities come from Iranian media reports and ship-tracking data cited by the Journal and CBS News.

What the boardings found

Both attacks occurred while the vessels were transiting the Strait of Gibraltar in early August. Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency reported that the VL Prosperity was attacked on August 7, losing communications for 30 hours, and — citing an unnamed crew member — alleged the attackers infiltrated engine-room systems, reduced engine cooling flow, and interfered with fuel and lubricating-oil systems. The Journal said it could not independently confirm that report.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=atXGYC6kPEw

The boarding team combined Coast Guard law-enforcement personnel, a vessel inspector, Coast Guard Cyber Protection Team members, and FBI Cyber Action Team operators. Rear Adm. Amy Grable, commander of Coast Guard Cyber Command, said cyber teams spent three to four days aboard each vessel doing incident response across operational technology and information technology systems, working with crews and corporate operators to "oust the threat."

"Unfortunately, many ships' IT systems are interconnected with other systems on a ship — the systems that control the engineering plant, propulsion, navigation, et cetera. So if those systems can be breached and controlled, then the crews could lose control of the vessel and it could cause a mishap or a collision."

— Rear Adm. Amy Grable, commander of Coast Guard Cyber Command, to the Wall Street Journal

Iran link under investigation

The Journal reports the U.S. is investigating whether Iran is behind the two attacks, citing officials familiar with the probe — raising concerns Tehran is seeking novel ways to widen its conflict with the U.S., possibly including disruption of a U.S. port. Attribution remains unconfirmed: the joint FBI–Coast Guard statement of September 16 named no culprit, and the Coast Guard and FBI declined to say how many cyberattack cases they have investigated since the war with Iran began. The backdrop is the active U.S.–Iran conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, in which Iran has attacked commercial ships attempting to transit without permission, prompting U.S. retaliation.

No damage — this time

"Currently, there are no reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts," the joint statement said, via the Associated Press. Crews cooperated fully and were called "critical partners" in mitigation. HMM Ocean Service, the South Korea-based technical manager of the VL Prosperity, told Bloomberg the tanker has "rigorous cyber protocols in place" and has been cleared for normal operations; it is idling off Galveston awaiting a final investigation report.

What comes next

The incident spotlights chronic weaknesses across global shipping: an earlier Journal investigation found Coast Guard teams boarding seized "dark-fleet" tankers and discovering pirated, malware-laden software and persistent remote-access tools on ship systems. With the FBI's Cyber Action Team now joining boardings, Washington is treating attacks on commercial vessels as a national-security investigation rather than a routine safety matter. What investigators conclude about attribution will determine whether this was criminal opportunism or a new front in the U.S.–Iran conflict — and for India, which moves most of its energy imports by sea, the breached IT/OT systems are the same ones running its crude carriers.
